source_locator.description: The lame man who had gone outside returns.

notes: The source role label `நொண்டி` is descriptive; the English stage direction does not use later continuity to assign a personal identity.
translation.english_text: (The lame man, who had gone outside, returns.)

notes: The vocative source form `இராகவா` is transliterated as `Iragava` rather than normalized to a nominative personal name.
translation.english_text: Iragava, is there anything special today?

notes: The verified source opens with `பாலம்`, retained as `Baalam` rather than silently corrected.
The form `இரங்கூனிலேன்னுமன்று` is pressure-sensitive; the surrounding syntax supports the Rangoon/brothers question, but the Tamil itself is not repaired.
translation.english_text: Baalam. A beggar woman came with a child. She asked who all of us were. We said we had been earning in Rangoon and were coming back... She asked whether we knew her elder brothers in Rangoon. We said we didn't.
What did she say her name was?

notes: The apparent mismatch with the following names is retained from the verified source rather than reconciled.
translation.english_text: That doesn't even seem like a Tamil Nadu name, does it?
Did she say Chandrasekaran, Gnana Sekaran, Guna Sekaran?

notes: The embedded fall is part of the immutable dialogue record and remains inside the same English unit.
translation.english_text: Ayyo, Kalyani! My younger sister Kalyani! Kalyani! (Crying out, he falls down.)
